Friday was a strong session for Jaleel's book, driven by a sharp +9.46% surge in Rocket Lab (RKLB), the largest single-day contributor given its 16.6% weight — by far the biggest position. The problem: RKLB carries an AVOID verdict and a QARP score of just 39.3, the weakest in the book. That kind of gap between price action and thesis is a flashing yellow light. ServiceNow (NOW, +6.42%) and Uber (UBER, +6.46%) also had strong days, with both benefiting from broader software and consumer-tech tailwinds; Palantir's upbeat results appear to have lifted sentiment across the space. NVDA added +2.27%, a steady contributor that continues to recover, while SAP (+3.36%) and Equifax (+3.85%) were quiet but solid.

The day's clear drag was Zoetis (ZTS, -5.97%), which slid to a -7.7% unrealized loss — the deepest loss in the book. ZTS carries a STRONG BUY verdict and an 84.6 QARP score, meaning the model and the price are firmly diverging. That divergence is worth watching, not panic-selling. Abbott (ABT, -0.14%) was essentially flat despite a mild EPS risk flag still hanging over it.

Two structural concerns deserve ongoing attention heading into next week: RKLB's weight relative to its conviction rating is the most acute mismatch in the book, and ZTS is now underwater with no fundamental justification visible in the data. BSX sits at a modest +1.8% gain but has an elevated guidance-cut flag with flat growth guided through Q3 — that's a holding where the thesis is quietly eroding.

attention.headline: Largest weight carries lowest conviction — +9.46% pop widens the mismatch
attention.note: At 16.6% of the book with an AVOID verdict and a QARP of 39.3 (lowest in the portfolio), Friday's spike makes the position even harder to justify on a capital-preservation mandate; the gap between price enthusiasm and model conviction has never been wider.

attention.headline: STRONG BUY/84.6 QARP now sitting at a -7.7% loss after -5.97% Friday
attention.note: Price and thesis are moving in opposite directions — the model rates this the highest-quality name in the book, yet it's the deepest loser; the divergence either resolves as a buying opportunity or signals that something fundamental has changed and needs to be identified.

attention.headline: Elevated guidance-cut flag with flat growth guided through Q3
attention.note: The STRONG BUY verdict hasn't been revised down, but FY26 growth cut from 10.5% to 7–8.5% with management guiding flat through Q3 means the thesis is carrying real execution risk until the October 20 report.

attention.headline: High-multiple software name surged +6.42% on sentiment, not new fundamentals
attention.note: Friday's move appears tied to Palantir-driven industry optimism rather than NOW-specific news; at its weight and multiple, any hawkish Fed repricing of software would make NOW the first and hardest-hit name in the book.
